utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I remind you of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Now, Mr. Smith, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, we left off yesterday when you stated that you were taken to Sremska Mitrovica and you left there -- you were taken away from there on the 4th of February, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at Sremska Mitrovica for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: There seems to be a misunderstanding about this. Can you please repeat the previous question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that you arrived at Sremska Mitrovica in November 1991, and can you tell the Court how long you stayed there and approximately what date you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, it appears that it is correct that I spent the period up until the 4th of February 1992 in Sremska Mitrovica. After that I was transferred to the military investigations prison in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you gave -- when you were at Sremska Mitrovica, were you interviewed by an investigative judge from the Belgrade court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was that interview about, briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: In actual fact, there was a series of interviews, but essentially they all focused on my involvement in Vukovar's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you taken to after Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: As has been mentioned, I was taken to the military investigations prison in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long were you detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I was detained until the exchange on the 14th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And before the exchange on the 14th of August, were you accused and placed on trial of the crime of armed rebellion and crimes against humanity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. Charges were brought against me. First a trial was announced and the next time around there was a trial that actually began, but was stopped at one point and we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you testify on the 11th of August, 1992 at that trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. I testified as an accused though.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know why the trial was stopped at one point and not proceeded with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: You mean the one that was first announced and then cancelled or do you mean the other one that was actually interrupted?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The one in which you testified on the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know the reasons for the interruption. However, the trial was interrupted and I told you what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then after being released from prison, did you return to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Zagreb was not my original place of residence. I was sent back to Zagreb. You can hardly call that a return.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise, that was my mistake. When you were in Zagreb on the 20th of August, 1992, did you give a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Soon after my release from captivity I did give a statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then on the 13th of March, 1993 did you give a statement to some Canadian investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement to some Canadian investigators also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then on the 14th of June, 1995 did you give a statement to Tribunal investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, the Tribunal investigators too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then did you give a second statement to the Tribunal investigators on the 14th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I did. The statements were recorded. I'm not sure about the dates; I shall take your word for it. But I did give a number of statements, more than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you also give a statement in 1996, in April 1996, in relation to an investigation -- investigative judge and the trial of Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. I gave that statement in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And also do you agree that you testified at this Tribunal on three occasions prior to coming on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would now ask that Exhibit 156 be placed on the screen, please. And if that could be enlarged one level higher, please. And if it can be moved up the screen a few centimetres too, please, to the top of the map. Thanks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this map in front of you, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is a geographical map of Vukovar, the town or the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you testified that you laid some mines on the confrontation lines when you commenced your job about the 14th or 15th of September, 1991. Are you able to draw an approximate line as to where those lines of confrontation were, just approximately? And if you take your time to do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Fine. [Marks]. Excuse me, there is something I have to point out. The map is rather small, or, rather, the scale is rather small, so this is a rough depiction of the lines. That's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We understand that. And this reflects what you believe to be some of the confrontation lines at what period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is in relation to October and November. Late in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday that as -- as the attack on the town ensued, that the lines -- some of the lines shifted towards the centre of the town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's right. The free area was getting smaller and smaller by the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And at these new confrontation lines, as the free area became smaller and smaller, did you lay mines at those locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, it was necessary at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 240.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Witness, you mentioned that -- I can see from the exhibit that you have a confrontation line near the JNA barracks. Can you tell the Court, when you took up your position, in mid-September, whether the JNA barracks was in the hands of the Croatian defence or the JNA and the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: As far as I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies for interrupting my learned friend, but this is a twice leading question, in a manner of speaking. Nobody ever mentioned that it was in the hands of the Croatian forces to begin with. On the other hand, it's quite leading to say that it was in the hands of the JNA and paramilitary forces. I don't think the witness can testify to this. And I think the OTP is just trying to pin this on this particular witness, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, your question is not as it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps we can approach it another way. If we can call for Exhibit 156 again in the original form, and then perhaps if we can enlarge it a couple of sizes, please. And if we can enlarge it perhaps one more, one more level. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you drew a confrontation line that was near the JNA barracks in the previous exhibit. Now that this is enlarged, can you draw the confrontation line again that was near the JNA barracks on the last exhibit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Confrontation line. Do you mean just the barracks or the entire thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you could draw the confrontation line that existed near the barracks, the one that you drew on the other map, when you first took up your post in September.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And just to be clear, these confrontation lines reflect what period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is in relation to October and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 241.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can call for Rule 65 ter number 228, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, this is a series of photographs that I would like you to comment on as we -- as we look at each one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: The Vukovar Hospital building. View from Gunduliceva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is ERN number 0053-1231-A. If we can go back to that original photo, please. Witness, are you able to say where the buses were parked when you got on them or got on one of them on the 20th of November, on that map [sic]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. They were on Gunduliceva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with the pen can you just draw a line to the approximate location of those buses, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And on that photograph can you see the exit or entrance that you left when you went towards those buses? And if you can, can you mark that with an X, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with the letter A can you mark the exit or entrance that you left when you left from the hospital, from the inside of the hospital to the outside, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I understand. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you also mark with a double line the place where you were searched as you were heading towards the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, please. This is ERN 0053-1232.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is Gunduliceva Street, facing the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we can look at the next photograph, please. 0053-1233. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the road that leads up the right-hand side of that photograph, what road is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's the street that we mentioned, Gunduliceva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the hospital, do you see that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you ring the hospital, please? Sorry, if just the usher could assist with the pen, please. Thank you. If you could place a ring around the hospital, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I ask that we now move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, we had a slight technical error when we marked the previous photograph. So could you, with a line again, draw the location of the buses, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with the letter A could you place that at the location of the exit in which you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with two double lines can you show the location of where you were searched before you were placed on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that letter X, does that depict the location from where you left the hospital grounds and went to the buses? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received as Exhibit 242, in place of the faulty one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I ask if we could move to photograph number 5, please. It should be ERN number 0053-1234. My mistake. Perhaps photograph number 4, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is a picture of the bridge across the Vuka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to photograph 5, please. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, that's the inner centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the bridge that you saw on the previous photograph, could you mark that with an X, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with an arrow, can you draw the direction of the hospital, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 244.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The previous photograph, you didn't tender? Was that intentional?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely. I think really I'd like to tender the whole package in addition to the ones that were marked. If we can go to the next photograph, please. This is 0053-1236.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, can you indicate any of those -- any of those buildings in the centre of that photograph? And what does that photograph generally describe or show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: You can see the centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And are there any particular buildings in the centre that you can recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I can recognise most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recognise the Danube Hotel in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, you can see the Danube Hotel. Should I indicate where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark that with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recognise the post office in that photograph? And if you can mark that with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you see the municipal building in that photograph? And if you do, if you could mark that with a C, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. I've marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And also can you recognise, I think, the defence building in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark that with a D, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that building is a separate building to the municipal building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: The buildings are across from each other. It's on the very edge of the photograph, perhaps you cannot see the municipal building, but they were about 10 to 15 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was the municipal building the headquarters of the Croatian defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: No. The municipal building was not the headquarters. The headquarters was in the old military department building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is that building on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, you can see a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark that with an E, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was the defence building the same as the old military department building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, it's in the same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the defence building, what was that being used for during October and November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's where the Vukovar defence command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, I am somewhat confused. We have three markings. Are they three distinct buildings? C, D and E? Or are there two buildings? Could that be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, it's a little bit unclear, and I may have made it unclear myself. But are there two defence buildings or, in fact, is it just the one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: There was one part of the defence ministry. However, inside that compound there was several buildings. But as far as the military sector, military department was concerned, that was one position. And then there was the other position, and that was next to it. So the two positions were alongside each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were -- sorry, both those buildings were in the same compound; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I'm talking about both of these areas. One of them was the military part, and the other part belonged to the municipality. Both the municipal and the military departments had their own buildings. I'm only talking about the military, the recruitment office that was in one area, and the municipal offices were next to that. So these were several buildings that were next to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, perhaps if I asked. You have marked as a C the municipal office. Is that in a building that is entirely distinct from the buildings marked D and E?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are completely separate buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The buildings marked D and E, are they also separate buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Each building is separate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, the old military department is building E; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: During October and November, or September, October and November 1991, what was building E used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was used as the command for the defence of the town of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in that -- at that same time, what was building D used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For military purposes also. Because it was part of the recruitment office. The buildings marked as D and E are actually one whole. It was the area that used to be used by the recruitment office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, 0053-1237, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Witness, looking at this photograph, do you recognise that? And, if you do, can you explain briefly what it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: You can see the centre of Vukovar again. You can see the hotel, the post office, the public accounting service. You can see the high-storey building. You can see the market. You can see the old workers' hall. You can see the Zagreb Nama department store building. You can see the rowing club. Also the three bridges across the Vuka River, and also the delta of the River Vuka, when it flows into the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark the location of the market with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark the post office with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark the public accounting service with a C, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that you could see the high-storey building. Can you mark that with a D and tell the Court what that was being used for during October and November 1991, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. I don't know to what purposes the building was used. All I know is that it was very damaged in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you also said you could see the Zagreb Nama department store. Could you mark that with an E, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the rowing club, can you mark that with an F, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the old workers' hall, could you mark that with a G, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I think this is looking at Vukovar from the opposite direction of the previous photograph. Can you see the municipal building on this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: You can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other central or public or obvious locations that you can see on that photograph that you can point out to us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: There is an Orthodox church here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark that with an H, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. It was the occupational training school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And are there any other public facilities that you can identify on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: There was the old pensioners' home or settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark that with an I, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. The Danube Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you could mark that with a J, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you see a large building to the right of the Danube Hotel in the centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know what that building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know which building you mean, but it's a little bit hard to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if you can just let us know whether there are any other locations that would be publicly known in this photograph that you can identify. Or have we run out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I mentioned the school, the occupational training school. That wasn't marked, especially. In the centre of town there were mostly shops. There were no large companies or buildings of any particular cultural significance in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark the occupational training school with a K, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said in the centre of town there was mostly shops. Is there an area in that photograph where those shops are congregated specifically or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It's hard to tell from this angle, but you could tell approximately where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if you can try and place a circle around the area of where these main shops are, or were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And those shops, were they the central shops for the town, the main shops for the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Well, you could conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 246, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, 0053-1238, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is Zmaj Jovanovica Street in Vukovar at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when we look at this photograph, looking forward, are we heading away from the centre of town or towards the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is leading in the direction away from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1239. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. It's the continuation of street that flows into Krasova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And as we look at the photograph, does it head away from the centre or towards the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It leads away from the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1240. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is the far end of Krasova Street leading from the centre of town towards Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1241. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is the crossing of Krasova Street and Sajmiste, and then the road runs on towards the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow on the photograph to indicate the direction of the barracks, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 247, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1242.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what area does it generally show, and are there any locations within that photograph that you can identify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is an area known as Sajmiste, and this is the crossing that we looked at a while ago. The cemetery is here, the firemen's hall, the health centre, and the rest are private homes for the most part. But you can also see the Stjepan Supanc school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Could you mark the crossing that we saw in the previous photograph with the letter A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you draw with an arrow, the direction of the JNA barracks, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark with a B the cemetery, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the firemen's -- Witness, it appears that you've marked two place was a B; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Correct. Two cemeteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark with a C the health centre, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with a D, the Stjepan Supanc school building, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other particular locations of a public nature that you can see in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I mentioned the firemen's hall too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark that with an E, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 248, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photo, please, 0053-1243.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the picture in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is the barracks in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that the buses or the bus that you were on and the other buses were taken to the barracks and you parked inside in a circle. Are you able to draw, with a line, the general location of where those buses were parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 249.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1244.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph are you able to recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is the path leading into the barracks from Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can look at the next photograph, please. This is 0053-1245. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. That is the barracks reception facing Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can look at the next photograph, please, 0053-1246. If this can be enlarged one level, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think we had 247, that number in the photograph, a while ago, and maybe my learned friend could check if the correct photographs are being shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, thank you very much. The error was just being spotted at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we can look at 0053-1246, please. It should be the previous one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this area in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the general area is, and if there is any particular buildings that you can identify within that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is the far end of Sajmiste Street, outside the town itself. In actual fact, it's the road to Negoslavci. This is the Vupik building. They produce drinks. The other building is the old railway station. It's called Vukovar Stari. And the brick works, Vukovar's brick works, the brick factory itself. You can see part of the Velepromet compound, their warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you could mark the Vupik factory with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the old railway station with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the brick factory with a C, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the part of the Velepromet compound that you can see with a D, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with an arrow, can you show the direction of Negoslavci, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 250, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can call for 0053-1247, thank you. The next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to identify the area in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I assume that this is the road between Vukovar and Negoslavci, but it's difficult to say which is where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can look at the next photograph, 0053-1248, please. It may be difficult, Witness, but can you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It's not easy, but I suppose that this is the junction along the Vukovar-Negoslavci road, and this must be -- the road that's forking off is the road leading to that farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you able to show the direction of Negoslavci on this photograph? And if you can, can you mark that with an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I may be wrong about this, but I think it's like this. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 251, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we can show the witness 0053-1249, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to recognise the area in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is an area between the town of Vukovar. If you take the side roads, and then you eventually end up at the Ovcara farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you able to indicate the direction of Ovcara with an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I'll do my best. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 252, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, 0053-1250, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the area depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I do. This is the Ovcara farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you draw a ring around the Ovcara farm, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said you were taken off the buses at Ovcara. Can you draw a line locating the approximate place where the buses parked, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks]. Perhaps around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise the hangar that you were taken into, that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's possible. I'm not positive from this angle, but it might be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. We understand that it would be an estimation at this stage, but can you mark the place where you think it is, please, with an A?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you able to mark the route that you took when you were placed on the military truck before you jumped off? If you can do it on this photograph, could you mark it? If not, we can go to another photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Witness, you've marked that photograph with an X. What does that X represent, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is where I might have jumped off that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour. And I ask that this one be tendered confidentially, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just from the point of view that this witness may be identified in relation to other people that might know that he was the witness that jumped off that truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Too big a shot, I think, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, we'll leave it then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 253, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I could ask for the next photograph, please. This is ERN number 0053-1251.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Ovcara farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you see the hangar in which you were placed at Ovcara? And if you do, could you mark it with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if are able, can you mark the route that the military truck took before you jumped out of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 254, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, how many more of these are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would say, Your Honour, about another five or six, and then we're finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we might adjourn now and resume after the break. It's necessary to make two adjustments to our normal programme today. First, it will be necessary for this break to be for half an hour, so that we will resume at 10 minutes past 4.00. Secondly, because of a meeting with some other Judges at 6.30, it will be necessary for us to adjourn for the night at about 6.25. That's unavoidable, I'm sorry about that. So that we will have a shorter two sessions when we resume at 10 past 4.00, and with a break somewhere around 5.10, 5.15, and then carrying on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, among the number of things that proved a bit of a set-back during that break for me, and I'm sorry that one matter delayed us, I am also told that one of the exhibits marked by the witness did not take electronically and will need to be redone. It was, I think, Exhibit 241, the main confrontation lines on the Exhibit 156 map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On the witness's arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that was the second map that he marked, the large version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: For a moment, I thought the Defence had a secret button to unmark the map, but I've spoken to them and I believe they haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think you can blame the Defence, Mr. Smith, nor yourself, nor us. I don't yet know why we lost two but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think e-court is good, Your Honour, it's just a little bit cumbersome on some occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we moved from one enlargement to another before it was tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps if -- I'll ask the witness to remark that one after we finish this series of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you see in front of you photograph 0053-1252, if you look at that photograph on your screen, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And on this one, if could you put a ring around the hangar that you were taken into, and perhaps mark with an arrow the entrance to the hangar in which you were taken, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And just a ring around the hangar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 255, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at the next photograph, 0053-1253.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that photograph in front of you, and do you recognise what it's a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In order for the witness to be able to answer this question, maybe he should first be told when this photograph was taken, which year, in view of what we can actually see in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has had in mind getting that clarified when we reached the end of this batch. It seems fairly clear that they are photographs some years after the relevant events. But I don't know that the actual year will help the witness. Carry on, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will provide that information at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is the hangar in question, and we're looking at it from the inside, and towards the door leading to the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this door, was this the door that you came in, or another one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in the photograph we can see some tractors and farm machinery. Was that machinery inside the hangar when you arrived in it, and perhaps if you could explain again other than the people in the hangar, was there any machinery in the hangar when you arrived there on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, that's a complex way of going about it. If this photograph was taken at the time of the others, it's clearly some years after the events. We can hardly take the photograph as evidence about machinery at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I ask that we look at the next photograph, which is 0053-1254.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, do you recognise -- do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the hangar at Ovcara, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I ask that we produce 0053-1255. Witness, are you able to recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It's similar to the one before. This is, I assume, the hangar at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And I ask that we look at 0053-1256. If that could be enlarged one level, please. And if it can include a little bit more of the right-hand side. Thank you. And, Witness, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It would be better if you could zoom in a little bit more. No, no, it's not necessary, actually. I recognise what this is now. I can see what the position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what does it depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This is the Ovcara farm, and this is a broader image of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the photographs in -- the whole group of photographs, the 26, in an unmarked form. I'm just getting confirmation, but I believe these photographs were taken in 1997, under the direction of an investigator at the Tribunal by someone from outside of the Tribunal. And I have the information here that the photograph album was made by Andrew Wright. He's the head of the photographic unit in the U.K., and the photos were taken under the supervision of the investigator working on the case in July 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The 26 unmarked photographs will be received as a group exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 256.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would ask that we go back to Exhibit 156, which is the map of Vukovar, and if we can enlarge it two levels, please. That should suffice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this map of Vukovar again, unfortunately the markings that you made in relation the confrontation lines in October, November 1991, they weren't recorded on the exhibit earlier, so we apologise, but we just ask, if you can take your time again, and mark the confrontation lines that you were first aware of when you took up your position with the defence of the town. And please take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would just like to help both the witness and the Prosecutor. We're talking about the continuous line that the witness drew, so he doesn't need to mark each individual line. So we're talking about the full line with which you indicated all the lines of defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark the confrontation lines, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Witness, if we look at the confrontation line by the JNA barracks, can you explain whether that line is going through the barracks or whether it's on the centre of Vukovar side, or on the Negoslavci side of the JNA barracks, if you can just clarify. It's a little bit difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: The line of confrontation or separation was between the barracks and the town. It actually went through the middle of the town. The front lines were also on the approaches to the town at Mitnica, Borovo Naselje, Borovo Selo, towards Brsadin. They went through the town itself as well as around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's clarified that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it should be received as Exhibit 241 in the place of the one that we tried before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's the number. And the next exhibit I'd like to show the witness is exhibit number 103, which is the map of Eastern Croatia. If we can have the bottom half of the map showing, please, from Vukovar down to the end. And if we can enlarge it one further layer, please. I think that's good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, this is a map of Eastern Croatia, showing the southern part. Do you see Stari Jankovci on the map, the place where you were taken before you were taken to Sid, then Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you circle that village, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were first detained in a village called Ceric. That village doesn't appear on the map. Can you tell us about how far away Ceric is from Stari Jankovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Perhaps a few kilometres. Three or four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And would that be three to four kilometres towards Vinkovci or Vukovar or further south?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Towards Vukovar. From Stari Jankovci towards Vukovar, some five -- four to five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 257, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, Witness, yesterday you told us some of the people that you identified as being detainees in the hangar at Ovcara, and you mentioned about seven or eight names, and then you said it was difficult for you to remember the other names at that time, but you would be able to perhaps identify them if you saw a list. We'll now produce to you a list of people, and if you can have a look at that list and go through it page by page, and mark anyone that you may have seen at -- you did see at Ovcara. And if you can mark the page and then hand that page to the usher and then that will be shown on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the annex to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if you can underline the name, and if we need a pen, it might be better.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I have a question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Is it just in the hangar, or also when I was taken away?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Also when you were taken away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to say something. The person next to whose name I wrote Kemo, I assume that that's the person who was very close to me in the hangar. So I wrote their nickname next to the name. I think that's the name and nickname that go together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to clarify: The names that you have underlined in red, they are people that you saw at the hangar and include the people that were taken on the military truck to the direction of Grabovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at page 3 that you marked. And is there anyone on that list that you can identify that you saw at the hospital before you were taken to the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Gudelj was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark alongside of his name with, say, a VH, the initials, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And you if could look at page 4 of the annex, is there anyone else on that page that you saw at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can look at page 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Mandic, Marko was a staff member at the hospital. I saw him at the hospital often.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would just like you to mark any name of anyone that you saw at the hospital on the 20th of November, or between the 19th and the 20th. Thank you. Witness, I noticed the name of Marko Mandic, you had the letters VH and then you crossed the initials out. Does that mean that you didn't see him on the morning of or the evening before the 19th to the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not sure that I saw him there that day, but he was a member of staff, so I saw him during that period. But I really am not sure whether I saw him on that exact day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you've testified that you left the Vukovar Hospital on the 20th of November, and in a number of your prior statements you state that you may have left on the -- you may have left on the 19th and arrived at the hospital on the 18th. Are you uncertain about the date that you arrived at the hospital and left the hospital? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Well, in a way there was a dispute whether it was the 18th, the 19th or the 20th. But the way things seem, in actual fact, I arrived in the hospital compound on the 19th, and it was on the 20th that we were taken away from the hospital. And I spent a total of one night at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Smith. Did you mean to tender the marked list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 258.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all. My learned friend has tendered this list into evidence, and one thing I would like to ask him is to provide copies, if possible, for the Defence teams, the ones marked by the witness, since we don't have those.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Let me introduce myself. I'm Miroslav Vasic on behalf of Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you too, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: There is one thing I would like to ask you before we start. We both speak a language that we understand. Since there are protective measures in place for you, please make a break after each of my questions. There are two reasons for this: Firstly, to keep your voice from carrying over my microphone and give me sufficient time to switch my mic off; the other reason being to give the interpreters sufficient time to interpret everything that is being said in its entirety, so that everybody else in the courtroom knows exactly what transpires between the two of us. Thank you. You testified in chief about a number of statements that you gave. You confirmed what he put to you. I want to ask you several questions that were not encompassed by my learned friend's questions. On the 27th of April, 2004 at the municipal court in Zagreb, were you not heard by the investigating magistrate of the district court in Belgrade in relation to the so-called Belgrade Ovcara case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You testified yesterday about the late spring and early summer of 1991 when you heard explosions in Vukovar. You talked about that yesterday. What I would like to ask you: Did you at that time hear about some people disappearing from Vukovar, going missing, residents of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know about anyone disappearing. I didn't hear anything like that, but perhaps if you clarify. I'm not sure what you have in mind, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will try to substantiate. Were there rumours in Vukovar that certain people had been led away in the evenings and that all trace of them was lost? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I didn't hear a thing about anything like that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like now to move on to a topic which relates to this witness's position in September 1991. I fear that perhaps his identity may be in danger of being revealed, and I surmise that this might call for private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will move to private and see whether it's proven necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to this group that we have mentioned, did you know that there were other groups doing the same sort of job in Vukovar, laying mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know if there were any other such parallel groups, but I do know that there were groups laying mines, and my predecessor told me a thing or two about that. In essence, however, at individual positions there were people laying mines independently. I even think that the police, the MUP, had their own units in charge of similar work. But I'm not certain about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Within the scope of your tasks related to the laying of mines, did you ever hear of a person named Franjo Kracak? Was he one of the people going about the same tasks and assignments? Are you familiar with that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I wasn't familiar with this name at the time. I did meet the gentleman later on, but I really can't say what his activities were at the time. I didn't know then and I still don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your group based in the building of the occupational training school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the basement of the former occupational training school.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You say the former school. Does this mean that it was no longer an occupational training school back in 1991? If this was the case, what was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It was something like a social hall. Occasionally used as a disco. It was a building used by the young of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As the group was going about its activities, I assume that you got your explosives from the mine bases. Where exactly were these mine bases or storages that you used for your own explosives and for your own missions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: They were in warehouses and storages where mines and explosives were stored. This was in several different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to share with us what these locations were of these various warehouses? I'm talking about September, October and November 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: One such storage place was in the basement of Vukovar's high school. There were two more storage rooms along the street near the water-tower, and two more along the street leading to the high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were any of these storage rooms located in what used to be known as the JNA street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA street, that's near the water-tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said yesterday that those were anti-personnel and anti-tank mines which were standard weapons in the JNA. Do you know how the mines got to be there in those storage rooms and what quantity are we talking about? What was the quantity at the time when you became a member of that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from or the exact quantity, but there were quite a number of mines there. Several hundred, several thousands, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said that it was the defence commander of Vukovar personally who handed out missions and assignments to your group, having previously agreed those with certain local commanders and commanders that acted along certain defence lines. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The commanders of individual defence lines had to be familiarised with these activities in order to be able to know where mines were being laid on the one hand, and on the other to provide security for you as you were going about your assignments laying mines; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said yesterday that you kept records, didn't you? What I wish to know is whether you gave a set of your entire documentation to the defence commander and whether another set or copy was given to the commander of whichever defence line it was that the mines had been laid at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This would not have been possible at the time. It wasn't possible to have daily reporting or to send anything in writing to Jastreb on a daily basis. But each and every commander working along the confrontation line had the duty to report exactly on how many mines had been laid and where, and they had to report to Jastreb directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the commanders of certain defence lines were duty-bound to submit these reports. Do you know if the commanders of certain defence lines sometimes laid mines along their own stretches even without previously consulting the commander or one of your own group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I did have information to indicate that there were groups who determined their own areas and made decisions in relation to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if this is the right time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... interrupt mine-laying, Mr. Vasic, but if we've reached a convenient point we'll break now. And we'll resume at 25 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Sir, before the break we talked about some activities undertaken by the commanders of certain lines along their axis in respect of laying down mines. What I'm interested in is if they had their own stockpiles of mines which they used in order to block certain sections. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had their own separate sources or warehouses for mines, except for the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me when you took up your duties when the group started to operate? You explained that at one point the group laid down minefields along the Mitnica line, near the Resa restaurant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, amongst other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time was the commander in this section Mr. Soljic, Ivan Soljic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It's possible. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me where did you lay down minefields in Borovo Naselje along the line of separation. If you can recall, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This was, for example, in the area of Trpinja and Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your group also laid down anti-personnel and anti-tank mines in the Bogdanovci sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of Bogdanovci as well. I mean, it depends on the time period that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, this laying down of minefields in the direction of Bogdanovci, which month as this in 1991, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It was, I assume, sometime in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also laid down mines in Luzac and also in the cornfields around Luzac; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Yes, our unit did do that also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me whether this was also done in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When it laid down mines in the area of Bogdanovci, did your unit lay down mines in the cornfields and did you also lay down mines some -- in some areas of the Vukovar-Vinkovci road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: We did not lay down mines around the village of Bogdanovci. We did it around the settlement of Luzac, so it was in the direction of the village of Bogdanovac. As for the direction leading to Vinkovci, we did not lay down mines on the actual road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to take Exhibit 240. That's the map where you marked the lines, the front lines at the request of my learned friend. So using the map, could you indicate with crosses the positions of minefields in these sectors? Could you please use a different colour though? And can we also zoom in a little bit, this map, zoom in by one step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Don't you mean 241, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because I would like the witness to draw in the positions which are on the Mitnica-Luzac-Bogdanovci spots, so I would like to look at the previous map. I think that we can see it there. Later we will take the map 241 to indicate the minefields in the town itself. So can we zoom out for one degree, one step, as we had it at the beginning so that we can see? Perhaps we can start from Mitnica, as it is. Could the usher please give the witness a different colour marker?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And you, sir, can mark on the Mitnica line by crosses where you recollect the minefields were that your group laid down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Well, the map is a little bit small. I'm not sure if I will be able to do it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, maybe we can zoom in the map in the Mitnica sector. This is the lower right-hand portion of the map. And then we will take it section by section. Can you see it well now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Well, it's a little bit better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So could you please indicate with crosses where these minefields were in the Mitnica sector?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move to the next sector; that's the Sajmiste sector? This is the sector in front of the JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Very well. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now move to the left section of the map where we can see Luzac and Bogdanovci, and this middle part we will deal with on the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps in order to save this as an exhibit, maybe we could tender it as an exhibit. I don't know how much time we have before what the witness has indicated will disappear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 259.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a small comment. I think this cross-examination will become quite detailed, and it's not clear at this stage at what time-frame these mines were laid, and I'm just wondering for the transcript whether that could be clarified so that it's not confusing when we get to the end of all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the confusion has already started, Mr. Smith, with your evidence. And Mr. Vasic's will add to it. And when it's all over, I hope you will be able to show me how relevant it is to our issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because at the moment, it escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask the usher to move to the left section of the map where we could see Luzac and Bogdanovci; perhaps we can move to that section of the map now. Left section of the map. Can we move the map towards the right so that we can see the left section of the map? Very well. We need to move it a little more to the right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness to mark in the Luzac sector the minefields that were laid down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark the minefields in the Bogdanovac sector?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Vasic, one at least of the blue crosses that has just been marked seems to have no relationship to the previous red-line marking. Do you want to find out whether that is additional to the red line?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was in that general area, but I will be more specific. Sir, this blue cross that is outside of this red line, I would say it's somewhere below the Luzac neighbourhood, can you please tell us what it represents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: It's a minefield that is outside of the Luzac neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: It was outside of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: No, this was not strictly along the front line, but it was a place where a possible attack by the enemy forces was expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I think that the answer is now clear. Thank you very much. Now I would like to ask you to draw the minefields or indicate where the minefields were in the -- in the Bogdanovci area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: I already did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Oh, thank you. I didn't notice that. Can we move the map to the right a little bit, so that we can see Bogdanovci?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suggest that -- I would like to tender this map into evidence as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 260.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can we shift the map to the right so that we can see Bogdanovci? Thank you. A little bit more to the right, please. Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate now where the minefields were in the Bogdanovci sector?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot. Because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you. I will not be needing this map anymore. I would like to ask to see Exhibit 241 now. That's the other map. And while we're waiting to see that map, I would like to ask you the following, sir: These positions that you indicated at Mitnica, Luzac and near the barracks, when were these minefields laid, in which month in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-011
utterances.text: This was in the course of October and November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
